short: The unpopular union between Mary I and Philip of Spain forged a powerful, albeit brief, Catholic Anglo-Spanish alliance.
full:
Seeking to secure a Catholic succession and strengthen ties with the Habsburg Empire, Mary I arranged to marry Philip, the heir to the Spanish throne. The proposal faced fierce domestic opposition, culminating in Wyatt's Rebellion, as English nobles feared the country would be reduced to a Spanish dependency. The marriage took place at Winchester Cathedral in July 1554.

To mitigate English fears, Parliament drafted a strict marriage treaty stipulating that Philip would enjoy the title of King only during Mary's lifetime, could not appoint foreigners to English offices, and could not draw England into Habsburg wars. Despite these safeguards, the alliance inevitably entangled England in the Italian War of 1551–1559, leading to the disastrous loss of Calais to France. The marriage remained childless, and Philip spent little time in England, effectively ending the alliance upon Mary's death in 1558.
